title: Which angles prove two set square lines are parallel?
description: A set square slides along a line l, and a line is drawn along its upright edge each time. The two angles with l are marked and compared, and they decide whether the lines are parallel. Keeko doubts the lines because they start at different places on l.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal corresponding angles with a transversal make two lines parallel, and sliding a set square keeps that angle the same. Watch for students who judge two lines by where they start and not by the angles they make.

source: Draw a line l with a ruler. Slide a set square along l and d
video_script.why: The child sees that the angle of a sliding set square stays the same, so the two lines make equal corresponding angles with l.
video_script.substitution: the book's own drawing: a line l, a set square slid along it, two lines along its upright edge
video_script.anchor: a line l drawn with a ruler, and a set square sliding along it with a line drawn along its upright edge each time
video_script.wrong_answer: because they start at different places
video_script.wrong_move: judges whether two lines are parallel by where they start on l, and not by the angles they make with l
video_script.payoff_line: Equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel

final_answer.value: Yes, parallel: the corresponding angles are both 90°
final_answer.spoken: yes, the two lines are parallel, because the corresponding angles are both ninety degrees

maths_rules: the upright edge of the set square makes 90 degrees with l each time
l crosses both drawn lines, so l is the transversal and the two angles of 90 degrees are corresponding angles
90 = 90, so the corresponding angles are equal
equal corresponding angles mean the two lines are parallel
video_script.design: One line l, one set square drawn in two positions, two right angle squares in the same corner at the two crossings. The same drawing stays for the doubt.
